title: Malaysian Airline System 653
summary: Malaysian Airline System Flight 653 was hijacked as it descended toward Kuala Lumpur on 4 December 1977. Someone knocked on the cockpit door and one or more hijackers suddenly barged into the cockpit. The pilots were forced to cut off all communications. Investigators heard a series of gunshots on the cockpit voice recorder and concluded that both pilots were fatally shot, leaving the aircraft professionally uncontrolled until it impacted the ground at near-vertical angle at Tanjung Kupang, killing all 100 people aboard.
probable_cause: The aircraft was hijacked by person or persons unknown. Investigators concluded the hijackers incapacitated both pilots through fatal gunshots, resulting in uncontrolled descent and impact with the ground.

factors.evidence: The aircraft was hijacked by person or persons unknown.
Investigators concluded that both the pilot and co-pilot were fatally shot by the hijacker.
The pilots were forced to cut off all communications by one or more hijackers who suddenly barged into the cockpit.
The aircraft's trajectory became unrecoverable, resulting in its impact with the ground at a near-vertical angle at very high speed.

events.text: Someone knocked on the cockpit door and one or more hijackers suddenly barged into the cockpit.
The crew reported to Subang Tower that an unidentified hijacker was on board, and the tower immediately notified the authorities.
The crew radioed they were proceeding to Singapore, followed by a series of gunshots on the cockpit voice recorder.
The aircraft hit the ground at a near-vertical angle at very high speed, and there were no survivors.
